subject: Positivity and centering constraints in stan

messages.author: 9a88613f54ea8688
messages.subject: Positivity and centering constraints in stan
parts:
Hi Stan-users!

When coding the SCAM model from Pia and Wood in Stan, I run into a problem.
Knowledge of this model is not required. $X_s$ is a smoothing spline base,
stored as a NxK matrix. $\beta_s$ is an ordered vector of K coefficients 
(to simplify). The expected value of the regression is $X_s \beta_s$.

Now the problem comes if I want to center the smoothing spline and model the
intercept explicitly. Conceptually, what needs to be done is
1) Center the smoothing spline so its mean is always zero (using the QR
decomposition of $X_s^T 1$), yielding $X_c$ a Nx(K-1) matrix of a centered
smoothing spline base.
2) Build the full design matrix X from a column vector of ones and the $X_c$
matrix. The expectation is then $X\beta$. $\beta$ can be decomposed in the
intercept $\beta_1$ and a vector $\beta_c$ (which corresponds to the K-1
last components of the vector obtained by representing $\beta_s$ in a base whose
first component is the constraint).

My problem arises because I have two constraints, applied in different
bases. The first one is the ordering constraint in $\beta_s$, the second one is the
centering constraint of the spline base. Two options came to my mind,
none of which made it to the end.

A. In the parameters block define `ordered[K] beta_s` and `real beta_1`.
In the transformed parameters block, compute `vector[K] beta` and other
quantities.  It seems to me that doing so can cause the optimizer to have problems
because there is one coefficient of beta_s whose value is arbitrary, as its variation
will be absorbed by the others due to the subsequent centering constraint.

B. In the paramters block, define `vector[K] beta`. That will fix the
degeneracy, but now I don't see how I can ensure that the underlying
beta_s is ordered.

How do you code such a problem in stan?

thanks a lot for this great program, it's been otherwise a pleasure to use.

parts: Le 14/03/16 20:25, Ben Goodrich a écrit :

On Monday, March 14, 2016 at 5:20:54 AM UTC-4, Yannick wrote:
When coding the SCAM model from Pia and Wood in Stan, I run into a problem. 
Knowledge of this model is not required.

Can you attach the code for the two options that you tried. I had a little trouble following you just from the description.
I have no working code, and the script I'm working on is very complex and has a lot of functions unrelated to this problem. Here is some pseudocode

A. In the parameters block define `ordered[K] beta_s` and `real beta_1`.
In the transformed parameters block, compute `vector[K] beta` and other
quantities.  It seems to me that doing so can cause the optimizer to have problems
because there is one coefficient of beta_s whose value is arbitrary, as its variation
will be absorbed by the others due to the subsequent centering constraint.

The working script without explicit intercept:

data {
 int N; //number of points
 int K; //number of parameters for unconstrained spline
 int x[N]; //variables
 int y[N];
}
transformed data {
 matrix X_s[N,K];
 X_s[N,K] <- design_spline(x,K);
}
parameters {
 ordered[K] beta_s;
}
model {
 y ~ poisson(exp(X_s*beta_s))
}




Case A: from beta_s to beta

data {
  //same as before
}
transformed data {
 matrix X[N,K];
 X[,1] <- rep_vector(1,N);
 {
  matrix X_s[N,K];
  vector
  X_s[N,K] <- design_spline(x,K);
  X[,2:] <- center_matrix(X_s);
}
parameters {
 ordered[K] beta_s;
 real beta_1;
}
transformed parameters {
 vector[K] beta;
 beta[1] <- beta_1;
 beta[2:] <- center_vector(beta_s); //many-to-one mapping causing problems for optimizer
}
model {
  y ~ poisson(exp(X*beta))
}





Case B: from beta to beta_s

data {
  //same as before
}
transformed data {
//same as case A
}
parameters {
  vector[K] beta;
}
transformed parameters {
    //how to ensure that beta[2:] can be built from calling
    //center_vector on a ordered[K] ?
}
model {
  y ~ poisson(exp(X*beta_s))
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Positivity and centering constraints in stan
parts:
The centering we recommend in the manual:

parameters {
ordered[K] c_raw;
...
transformed parameters {
ordered[K] c;
c <- c_raw - sum(c_raw) / K;
...

isn't going to work well, because as you point out, it leaves
the underlying parameter c_raw unidentified because c_raw +/- constant
leads to the same centered vector.

An alternative is to sort

parameters {
vector[K - 1] c_raw;
...
transformed parameters {
vector[K] c;
c[1] <- -sum(c_raw);
c[2:K] <- c_raw;
c <- sort_asc(c);

but I don't think that works well for Stan because then the positions
of the vector c_raw aren't well identified. Maybe the c_raw could
itself be ordered to cut down on some of the uncertainty.

I'm afraid I don't have a good suggestion for a sorted, centered
sequence. Ben's really good at this, so hopefully he'll figure
something out.

- Bob

an open access license or you can point to an external source).
